title: Variant compatibility sweep and ops cadence for smart-routing fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Maintain and extend the fallback variant compatibility matrix used by smart-routing (region selection + tier routing). The goal is a reproducible, automated sweep that verifies tokenizer byte-level parity, KV-cache resume compatibility, and tooling/serving-contract parity for candidate fallback variants so that regional or tier-based automatic fallbacks do not introduce silent regressions.

Background: 
- Smart routing can automatically route requests to alternate model variants when capacity or region constraints apply. Fall back variants must behave deterministically with respect to tokenization, context length handling and runtime tooling (function calling, structured output, KV-resume semantics).
- We currently have a manually-curated compatibility catalog with gaps and aging metadata. Incidents: two customer reports where region fallback produced tokenization mismatches in non-utf8 prompt sequences (see incident notes).

Scope:
- Create an automated sweep job that validates each candidate fallback pair (primary -> fallback) across three axes: tokenizer parity (byte/ids roundtrip), context/seqlen semantics (prefix truncation/resume), and runtime tooling contracts (function-calling signatures, special tokens, structured JSON outputs, kv-cache resume).
- Integrate sweep results into the compatibility matrix in the registry and surface failure signals in Console (per-route model diagnostics).
- Add a weekly maintenance cadence with alerting for newly-detected regressions and a triage runbook.

Out of scope: fine-grained kernel performance regression checks (handled by perf team), or formal model quality evaluations (handled by Eval).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define a canonical `variant-manifest` schema with fields the router needs (tokenizer_hash, special_tokens_map_hash, max_context_effective, kv_resume_signature, supported_tooling_flags). Store manifests in the variant registry.
2) Build `compat-checker` CLI that runs three checks for a pair: tokenizer-roundtrip (sample corpus + edge cases), context-behavior (prefix + resume + truncation strategies), tooling-contracts smoke tests (function-call roundtrip + structured-output canonicalization). Produces a deterministic PASS/FAIL + diagnostics blob.
3) Author a CI job pipeline (infra: runtime repo) that runs compat-checker for every new variant upload and on a weekly sweep for older variants. Persist results to the compatibility matrix DB and emit telemetry.
4) Console integration: add a diagnostics tab that shows compatibility status per variant pair and provides actionable remediation (e.g., recommend quantized variant with matching tokenizer_hash or mark variant as `no-fallback`).
5) Rollout: Canary on internal staging region for 2 weeks; then enable for non-prod regions; finally flip on for low-traffic production tier with automatic rollback if compatibility anomalies spike.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated sweep runs on new variant uploads and weekly for registry, producing PASS/FAIL and diagnostic artifacts for each fallback pair.
- Tokenizer-roundtrip check catches and reports byte-level mismatches for at least 3 known edge cases (unicode combining marks, surrogate pairs, null-bytes).
- Console shows per-route fallback compatibility status and a direct link to diagnostics for any failing pair.
- Router consults the matrix during smart-routing decisions and respects `no-fallback` flags; verified by integration test harness (simulated regional failover).
- Alerting created: when the sweep detects a previously-PASSed pair moving to FAIL, on-call list is notified and ticket template is created.

Deliverables / Tasks (owner in parens):
- Variant-manifest schema spec + conformance tests (Marco Chen).
- Compat-checker CLI prototype + unit tests (Marco Chen).
- CI pipeline + weekly scheduler + storage of results (SRE - see ENG-31207).
- Console diagnostics tab and link into per-route dashboards (Frontend - tracked in PM).
- Runbook and triage playbook for FAIL -> remediation (Aisha Patel).
- Integration test: simulated region failover exercising router decision path (QA/Infra).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: false negatives due to insufficient corpus. Mitigation: add targeted corpus from incidents and partner customers, expand fuzzing.
- Risk: slow weekly sweep if registry grows. Mitigation: incremental checks and prioritization by usage / traffic.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New metrics: compat_sweep_pass_rate, compat_pair_failures_total, compat_check_latency_seconds.
- Dashboard: http://metrics.redwoodinternal/variants/compat (canary + prod views).

Links / artifacts: 
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SmartRouting+Fallback+Compatibility+Spec
- Runtime PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2761
- Incident notes: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2025-017-fallback-tokenizer-mismatch

Notes: prioritize high-traffic primary variants and any variants used in Dedicated/Private deployments first (higher customer impact). This ticket pairs with ENG-31207 (CI scheduler) and ENG-24091 (variant manifest ingestion).
comments: 2025-02-14: Initial scoping review with PM and SRE. Agreed to prototype CLI and schema first. Action: Marco to drop schema RFC by 2025-02-18.
2025-02-20: RFC posted: Conformance tests for tokenizer_hash and special_tokens_map_hash included. Feedback from Research: add surrogate-pair fuzzing. Will include corpus from incident logs.
2025-02-26: Prototype compat-checker v0.1 uploaded to runtime repo (see PR #2761). Unit tests for tokenizer-roundtrip added. Marco requests review from Research and QA.

2025-02-28: QA ran integration harness on staging; found two KV-resume signature mismatches for quantized variant q4f-small -> q4f-tiny in region eu-west-2. Marked variant pair as FAIL and filed follow-up ENG-915001 to remediate KV layout.
2025-03-01: Planning meeting outcome: weekly sweep scheduled; canary rollout window reserved for 2025-03-10 to 2025-03-24. Aisha to author runbook draft by 2025-03-05.

Review notes (2025-03-01): PM suggests adding an automatic `no-fallback` tag when tokenizer mismatch is detected for any variant used in a customer route. Frontend requests API changes to surface diagnostic URLs in Console.
Next steps: finish triage runbook, add more corpus fuzzers, wire up metrics and alerting, schedule canary rollout.
